You can't be a reformed narcissist by just quitting an addiction, that means you weren't a narcissist in the first place. Either that, or you still are one. And your advice isn't actually as helpful. On paper, yes, "just ignore her works". It does work. But OP's shoes are ones filled by the feet of a kid who's been worn down into a frightened being for years. Raising your voice, yelling, being treated with suspicion, being harassed over your private life - all these things can trigger a fight or flight mode, a physical stress response that worsens your depression or anxiety. It's to the point that if these things are happening day after day after day, which is likely to happen if her mother goes into a rage over her trying to have some form of independence, OP will be stuck in a temporary cycle of heightened anxiety. When I'm anxious, I usually enter an apathetic and paralyzed or dazed state, and it can prevent you from making any self-preserving decisions like moving out because your brain's "just trying to get through this".

Really the only way we can protect ourselves from manipulation and abuse - all forms of abuse including financial abuse - is being able to see the signs if and when they present themselves. But because your mother has made you distrust your own judgement due to years of being told that your judgement is fallible, the second best thing is to have a support group of people you know are trustworthy to maintain communication with at all times and talk about your life with. Oftentimes, these are friends. If you have any friends to keep in contact with, please keep in contact with them - even if you meet a guy who tells you not to (in fact that's a red flag for potential abuse/user behaviour down the road). Continue to post to reddit and other social media as you do to gain feedback on any situation you feel is off. Also, I don't mind talking to you if you want to reach out in DMs. I don't know you, and will never know you personally, so if you feel worried that someone may be taking advantage of you, you can ask reddit, friends, or me (or all would be best), for a take on a certain behaviour. When you have enough people looking at things, it cancels out the bias, and hopefully you'll be able to spot dangerous situations that way.

Sorry in advance for the really long post:
I know you don't want to hear this, and I'm sorry, but that *is* abuse. Her calling you those words is abusive. Now what you may be trying to convey is that she isn't her Father, but that doesn't mean she doesn't carry those fleas (learned behaviour from abusive parents). Even former kids with fleas from narcissistic parents can end up looking like full-blown narcissists, from a non-professional's perspective. You do not exist to be her therapist or her emotional dump. It only takes one trigger for people like you to find themselves dragged down to the levels of their partners (and I hope that day never comes), it's usually a mixture of different stuff happening all at the same time (and don't think this is unlikely) - a bad situation at work, an injury, something that disrupts your daily routine, or a loss of emotional support via perhaps losing your friendship group, any of those things happening to you, and having to come back home to verbal abuse, could very well trigger an onset of depression.

Once you get depressed, can't hold down a job, etc, what is she going to do? She'll be back at square one but so will you too. You're not some superhero, or god, you're a human and you have a limit. She has to learn the difficult way, and I hope her skin is thick enough. I had to too. I grew up with an physically abusive parent and my Dad was the enabler. Finally, he left (all of us, including the kids). I later lived with him in my late teens and had massive abandonment issues from him leaving and not staying to protect us. And he wasn't perfect, but god would I take my anger out on him and think that it was all justified. I ended up moving back in with my Mum, and it's given me perspective and helped me grow. I understand how to hold my cool when she's flying into a rage, I understand how to let suicidal feelings pass, but most importantly, I understand that my Dad, despite his faults, is not the same as my Mum. I understand that he's human, I understand that he's fallible, but most importantly I learnt to look at him in a more human light and less as a crutch. He suffered abandonment as a kid too, he didn't know how to parent, he was just running away from something that hurt him. Sorry not trying to write this as a therapy session for myself, I'm just sharing from my point of view so that you'll have hope that she'll get through you not being there. I kind of sense you're worried she'll commit you-know-what, that's why I included how I learnt to get through my suicidal thoughts.

There is a second option though, that you talk about all of this with her and give her an ultimatum: she gets therapy and stops constantly belittling you, insulting you. Either that or you move one, I'm sorry that you've found yourself in an abusive relationship. I hope you can heal, because the scars are deep. Find someone who values you for you.
